purpose: Record which lane the gemma4 rows actually get on Windows by default, and what the execution plan says they get.
host: RTX 3060 Laptop GPU 6143 MiB / Windows 11 / 16 logical cores

row.note: Chosen over E4B Q8_0 (7.63 GB) deliberately: it is the largest gemma4 row that fits the 6 GB card, so it is the row Phase 3 can actually put resident.

observed.env: CAMELID_GEMMA4_CUDA unset (default configuration — no env overrides of any kind)
observed.model_bytes_on_gpu: none — 2.83 GB of weights stayed in host RAM

cadence.prompt: Name the capital of France in one word.

finding_plan_routing_disagreement.why: The generic execution plan is computed from platform + quant and reports the CUDA K-quant resident lane whenever CUDA is active. The gemma4 serve path does not consult that plan: resolve_gemma4_runtime picks Gemma4ServeRuntime::Cuda only when gemma4_cuda_enabled() is true, which requires CAMELID_GEMMA4_CUDA=1. Unset, it loads the CPU runtime while the plan keeps advertising the GPU lane.
finding_plan_routing_disagreement.proof: 107 MiB of VRAM in use while a 2.83 GB model generates. A resident lane cannot decode from 107 MiB.
finding_plan_routing_disagreement.relation_to_D20: This is the same class of defect DECISIONS D20 was written for in the Metal campaign — a plan that advertises a lane serve is not running. It is recorded here because Phase 3 changes exactly this gate, and the fix must make the plan and the routing agree rather than merely flipping the default.
finding_plan_routing_disagreement.scope: Observed for gemma4 on Windows/CUDA. Not investigated on other hosts or families in this phase.

not_claimed: No throughput claim. The single-token timing is an observation with no isolation discipline behind it.
No parity claim of any kind.
No claim about gemma4 E4B, 12B, or 26B rows.
